mission_07: Multivariate time series forecasting extends univariate methods by modeling the joint dynamics of multiple interrelated time series simultaneously. The Vector Autoregression (VAR) model is the most fundamental multivariate approach, where each variable is modeled as a linear function of its own past values and the past values of all other variables in the system. This captures the feedback relationships between variables that univariate models miss. Cross-correlation analysis reveals the lead-lag relationships between pairs of series at different time offsets, helping identify which variables are predictive of others. Granger causality testing formalizes this by comparing the predictive power of a restricted model (using only the target's own lags) against an unrestricted model (including lags of the potential causal variable). In this mission, you will implement cross-correlation computation, fit a VAR model using ordinary least squares on the stacked lag matrix, generate recursive multivariate forecasts, and perform Granger causality tests to identify predictive relationships between time series.
